title: engineering all-hands 2026-05-20
content:
Date: 2026-05-20
Attendees: engineering@redwood, SRE, product leads, recruiting
Owner/Facilitator: Asha Patel (platform eng)

Agenda:
- Quick metrics + wins (2m)
- Incident recap + action items (5m)
- Team updates (serving-runtime, infra, private-deployments, console) (15m)
- Roadmap highlights & upcoming milestones (8m)
- Hiring & org changes (2m)
- Q&A + shoutouts (3m)

High-level metrics / wins:
- 99.92% API availability last week (improvement after autoscaler tuning).
- Median tail latency for 2k-token workloads down 12% after kernel selection change (serving-runtime).
- Reduced per-token cost for typical chat workload by ~6% after rework of batching heuristics.
- Demo: private deploy on Azure gov completed for pilot customer (successful end-to-end tests).

Incidents / Reliability:
- Brief outage on 2026-05-18 (09:14–09:43 UTC) affecting a subset of Dedicated customers in us-west. Root cause: autoscaler race condition during a burst of provisioning requests causing a transient scheduler lock.
  - Mitigation: fallback routing to secondary pool activated automatically for affected customers.
  - Action items: (1) release hotfix to autoscaler to avoid lock (owner: Ravi Menon, due: 2026-05-22); (2) add more robust observability around provision queue length (owner: SRE team, due: 2026-05-28).

Team updates (highlights only):
- Serving Runtime (Marco Diaz)
  - Released kernel selection improvements (see PR #412). Early benchmarks show 12% tail latency reduction on mid-sized models.
  - Working on KV-cache memory leak fix; test coverage added. Expect rollout next week to canary pool.
  - Blockers: minor perf regression on 16-bit quant paths when sequence length > 4k. Engineering investigating.

- Infrastructure & SRE (Lena Thompson)
  - Autoscaler hotfix in progress; canary deployed to staging.
  - Capacity planning: provisioning schedule for end-of-Q2 spikes completed; reserve window booked with cloud partner.
  - Improving PagerDuty runbooks to reduce escalation blast radius.

- Private Deployments (Sofia Alvarez)
  - Azure Gov pilot passed compliance checklist — moving to paid pilot stage with customer legal.
  - Packaging improvements: shrink installer image and improve healthcheck behavior for air-gapped installs.

- Console & Observability (Ravi Menon)
  - New per-route latency breakdown dashboard in console is live in beta. Ask: product teams to try and provide feedback via the survey in console.
  - Backend trace sampling rate adjusted to reduce costs without losing signal.

Roadmap / upcoming milestones:
- End of May: Release autoscaler hotfix and KV-cache leak patch.
- Early June: Begin A/B rollout of new batching policy (opt-in for Dedicated customers).
- Mid-June: Private Deploy GA for Azure & first supported on-prem appliance test.
- Q3 planning: begin work on multi-region model pinning and cross-region failover policies.

Hiring & org notes:
- New hires this week: 2 SREs onboarded (welcome Megan Li and David Okafor).
- Recruiting: actively hiring for senior runtime engineer (req #ENG-321).
- Org: rotating meeting owners — platform eng all-hands will be co-facilitated by Marco & Asha next month.

Action items (clear owners & dates):
- Ravi: finalize autoscaler hotfix PR and merge to main (due 2026-05-21).
- Marco: finish regression test for 16-bit quant path and escalate to research if required (due 2026-05-24).
- SRE: implement provision queue observability (dashboard + alert) (due 2026-05-28).
- Sofia: share Azure Gov pilot feedback doc with product & legal (due 2026-05-25).
- All teams: test new per-route dashboard and submit feedback survey (due 2026-05-27).

Shoutouts & wins:
- Shoutout to infra on getting the reserve window negotiated under tight timelines — helped avoid potential capacity shortage.
- Thanks to runtime team for the kernel perf improvements and quick Canary turnaround.

Q&A summary:
- Q: Timeline for full rollout of batching policy?
  - A: Opt-in A/B starts early June, will measure cost/latency and expand gradually through June/July.
- Q: Is there a rollback plan for the private deploy GA?
  - A: Yes — GA will include automated snapshot & rollback tooling; we will run a canary and recovery drill during GA week.

Notes / links:
- Deck (speaker notes): https://drive.redwood/links/all-hands-2026-05-20
- Incident JIRA: JIRA-INC-2210
- Autoscaler PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/88

Next meeting: 2026-05-27 (same time).

Document notes: working notes captured during meeting; please add follow-ups as comments on this doc or link PRs/Jira tickets for closed items.
